newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Man killed in feud ahead of Pakistan election.
newsitem.headline: Man killed in feud ahead of Pakistan election.

text.p: The body of a young man, apparently the latest victim of pre-election factional feuding, was found in a park in the Pakistani port of Karachi on Friday, police said.
They said the 28-year-old man had been kidnapped, stripped naked and hanged. His face was burned beyond recognition before he was dumped in a small park in the Orangi Town district.
"The body had a burnt rope around the neck," a police officer said, adding that at least three political activists had been killed in Karachi in the past six days.
They died in clashes between rival factions of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) planning to contest national and provincial assembly elections on February 3.
President Farooq Leghari ordered the polls after he sacked Benazir Bhutto's government, alleging corruption, on November 5.
Ethnic, sectarian and political violence claimed more than 500 lives in Karachi last year, down from 2,000 in 1995.
Last Saturday a bomb blast in Lahore killed Zia-ur-Rahman Faruqi, leader of the militant Sunni Moslem Sipah-i-Sahaba Pakistan (SSP) organisation and a candidate in the elections.
The SSP accused militant Shi'ite Moslems of carrying out the explosion, which killed 26 people and wounded 90.
